externalTitle: Leadership and commitment; Roles, responsibilities and authorities; Internal organization
notes: 42001 establishes top-management direction and roles for the AI management system. AIDCF GOV-01 additionally requires decision rights over infrastructure Assurance Decisions, committee oversight of gates and ownership of the assessment methodology.

externalTitle: Roles, responsibilities and authorities; Internal organization
notes: Role assignment for the AIMS overlaps RACI and role ownership. 42001 does not address accountability for Required Functions of facility infrastructure, risk-acceptance authority for gate outcomes or evidence custody.

externalTitle: AI policy; Documented information; Policies related to AI
notes: Policy hierarchy and document lifecycle overlap directly. Technical Standard Baselines for power, thermal, compute, storage and network engineering are outside 42001.

externalTitle: Actions to address risks and opportunities; Internal audit; Management review
notes: Risk-based planning and review of the management system align with assurance planning and independent review. 42001 has no equivalent of Critical Gate governance.

externalTitle: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties; Information for interested parties of AI systems
notes: Interested-party requirements (including regulatory and customer obligations) overlap. Infrastructure customer commitments (availability, recovery tolerances) are not specifically addressed.
Competence overlaps. Conflict management, assessor independence and appeal are certification-body matters addressed by conformity-assessment standards rather than by 42001 itself.

A.4 expects the organisation to identify and document resources for AI systems, including system and computing resources. AIDCF CAP-01 requires a register of bounded Capability Instances with owners, lifecycle status and architecture linkage.

externalTitle: AI objectives and planning to achieve them
notes: AI objectives concern the AI system; AIDCF Service Outcomes (availability, performance, integrity, recovery with tolerances) are infrastructure outcomes that support them.

externalTitle: AI system impact assessment; Assessing impacts of AI systems
notes: Impact assessment of AI systems on individuals and society informs stakeholder consequence and criticality of the infrastructure supporting them. It does not define infrastructure impact tolerances.
Resource documentation may record current compute allocation. Demand modelling (peak, transient, growth, scenario) is not addressed.

externalTitle: Planning of changes; Operational planning and control; AI system life cycle
notes: AI system lifecycle controls (design, verification, deployment, operation) are a context for infrastructure commissioning acceptance and material-change impact, but do not address them.
Resource documentation can seed asset-to-function mapping. Upstream, downstream and recovery dependency mapping are not required.

externalTitle: Third-party and customer relationships; Operational planning and control (externally provided processes)
notes: Third-party relationships for AI systems overlap at objective level. Utility, telecom and OEM dependency of facility infrastructure is outside the AIMS scope unless deliberately included.

externalTitle: Determining the scope of the AI management system
notes: An AIMS scope statement is an input to, not a substitute for, the AIDCF assessment boundary, provider boundary and tenant boundary.

externalTitle: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation; Third-party and customer relationships
notes: General monitoring of the management system and third parties; no dependency health indicators or periodic revalidation of dependency maps.

aidcfFamilyName: Fire, life safety and emergency interfaces

notes: 42001 does not set energy-performance requirements; see EN 50600 and Singapore crosswalks.
Records of system and computing resources produced under A.4 can corroborate the compute inventory (E1 evidence). They do not establish architecture adequacy or an approved baseline.
Resource provisioning for AI systems is a context for usable accelerator capacity; scheduler controls and contention management are not addressed.
A.7 addresses data acquisition, quality and provenance for AI systems, not the storage tiers that hold training data, checkpoints and artefacts.
Data quality and provenance objectives are a context for storage data integrity; checksum, scrubbing and metadata integrity are not addressed.

externalTitle: Resources; Competence; Resources for AI systems (human resources)
notes: Resourcing and competence for the AIMS; no 24x7 coverage, shift handover or authorisation-to-operate requirements for facility operations.
Operational control of AIMS processes; method statements, permit to work and lockout/tagout are outside scope.

externalTitle: Nonconformity and corrective action; Information for interested parties of AI systems
notes: Corrective action and communication about AI system incidents to interested parties are a context for incident and problem management. Alarm rationalisation and infrastructure incident response are not addressed.
Planned change to the management system; configuration baselines and rollback for infrastructure are not addressed.
Generic performance evaluation; no capacity review or service-level monitoring of infrastructure.
Determination of internal and external communication; crisis command and emergency change are not addressed.
Supplier responsibilities for AI systems overlap with supplier due diligence. Financial and operational resilience and sub-tier visibility of infrastructure suppliers are not addressed.
Allocation of responsibilities with suppliers and customers overlaps service obligations. Evidence rights, incident notification and exit rights are not specified.
No hardware provenance, counterfeit prevention or component traceability requirements.

externalTitle: Resources for AI systems (tooling); Third-party and customer relationships
notes: Tooling and third-party resources are documented; release provenance, signature validation and vulnerability response for firmware are not addressed.
42001 relies on the organisation's information-security management for access control; use the ISO/IEC 27001 crosswalk.

externalTitle: AI system life cycle; Use of AI systems
notes: 42001 governs responsible use of AI systems, including human oversight objectives. AIDCF SEC-06 applies this to AI agents or automation acting on infrastructure: bounded authority, approval controls, command allowlisting and safe rollback, which 42001 does not specify.
Creation, control and retention of documented information overlap evidence taxonomy, repository and retention. 42001 has no evidence classes or quality model.
Document control supports integrity and custody; provenance, relevance, reliability and currency ratings (AIDCF-008 P/F/C/R/T/I) are not addressed.
Audit programme, criteria and scope overlap assessment planning. Decision questions, claim types and specialist technical testing are AIDCF-specific.
Nonconformities map to Findings. 42001 has no concept equivalent to UNKNOWN Records, conflict handling or limitation disclosure.
Management review takes decisions about the AIMS; it has no gate evaluation or bounded claim language.

externalTitle: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation; Continual improvement
notes: Ongoing evaluation and improvement overlap continuing assurance. Evidence expiry, change triggers and decision suspension are AIDCF-specific.
